notes: I could not run Python in this session. I only had WebFetch, and it returns small-model summaries, so I could not stream or sum base_count. The ENA Portal API is reachable with no login. The /count endpoint works with the query instrument_model="Illumina NovaSeq 6000" AND first_public>=2026-06-01 AND first_public<=2026-06-30. One query in the probe, first_public=2026-06-01 as an exact date, returned only the TSV header, so range queries are needed. Run counts for June 2026 are 162,732 for the NovaSeq 6000 and 26,507 for the NovaSeq X. That is about 86% / 14% by run count, which is already-known run-count work and not Gb. I did not compute Gb shares or quarterly series, and I have no new evidence items. ENA first_public reflects when submitters released data, usually 6-24 months after sequencing. It is dominated by academic deposits and many runs are small, so the mix will skew toward the 6000 and research. Any Gb-weighted share will lag Illumina's reported 17% and should be treated as a trend or slope signal only, not a level to compare against 17%.
how_to_mine: Run scripted. For each month 2024-01 to 2026-09 and each model (Illumina NovaSeq 6000, Illumina NovaSeq X, Element AVITI, UG 100, DNBSEQ-T7; check the exact instrument_model strings with a count query first), request /ena/portal/api/search?result=read_run&query=instrument_model="X" AND first_public>=YYYY-MM-01 AND first_public<=YYYY-MM-last&fields=run_accession,base_count,center_name&format=tsv&limit=0. Stream each response to a file in an empty directory, sum base_count in Python with -I, and add 1-2 s pauses between calls. Also run a second cut with the NovaSeq 6000 and NovaSeq X filtered to center_name values that are clinical or commercial labs, to separate them from academic deposits. Report the 6000 share of Illumina Gb and of total Gb by quarter, the AVITI+UG100 share of total Gb, and the slope of the 6000 share. If the downloads are too big, sample Mar, Jun and Sep of each year. Normalise by collection_date or last_updated if the first_public lag distorts the series.
